history.world-divided-effects.0006.all: Effect 1: Truman was more hostile/less trusting than Roosevelt; at Potsdam (July 1945) he was tougher with Stalin, and Stalin's suspicion grew, e.g. over Eastern Europe. Effect 2: Truman told Stalin of the atomic bomb / used it on Japan (Aug 1945) without consulting him, and later the Truman Doctrine (1947) / containment, which increased Soviet fear and the arms race.

history.world-divided-effects.0061.all: Effect 1: tensions eased - SALT 1 (1972) limited ICBMs and ABMs, slowing the arms race. Effect 2: improved contact/trade and summits, e.g. Nixon visited Moscow 1972, Basic Principles Agreement, Ostpolitik/Berlin agreement 1971-72; but rivalry continued in the Third World.

history.world-divided-impression.0012.all: Impression: Poland was the most bitter dispute, Stalin acted ruthlessly/cynically and the Allies were divided. Evidence: 'no issue caused more argument'; rival Lublin communists; Red Army halted at Warsaw and let the uprising be crushed.

history.world-divided-impression.0018.all: Impression: Germany increasingly divided, USSR vs West with conflicting aims (exploitation vs recovery); West moved unilaterally towards a separate state. Evidence: factories taken as reparations; Bizonia 1947; Deutschmark 1948.

history.world-divided-impression.0038.all: Impression: Wall built out of East German desperation to stop refugees/brain drain, with Ulbricht pushing Moscow; sudden and unilateral. Evidence: 'bleeding to death', 3 million fled, skilled workers, 30,000 in July, Ulbricht begged, barbed wire overnight.

history.world-divided-impression.0005.all: Impression: Yalta looked successful and friendly on paper but there were hidden weaknesses/doubts, especially over Poland and Soviet power on the ground. Evidence: friendly atmosphere, zones/UN/war on Japan, vague Poland promises, Red Army occupying.

history.world-divided-impression.0006.all: Impression: the Poland question was unresolved and vague, with Stalin holding the real power since the Red Army occupied it, so free elections were doubtful. Evidence: 'promises about Poland were vague', Red Army occupied, 'agreement on paper was one thing'.

history.world-divided-impression.0052.all: Impression: NPT was a rare, genuine superpower cooperation and a reciprocal bargain, widely accepted. Evidence: 'rare example', both wanted to stop spread, non-nuclear states promise not to build / nuclear powers share technology and disarm, 60+ signed.

history.world-divided-impression.0005.problem: Note only: identical extract to impression.0006 (different question, different mark scheme); not a fault.
